title: Geometric neutral-fibre reductivity is invariant under field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $L/k$ any field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $G$ be a smooth affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with no connectedness hypothesis. For an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], put $G_\Omega=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $G_\Omega^0$ be the connected component containing the identity, with its induced open-subscheme structure [def-weil-connected-scheme]. A smooth connected affine group over an algebraically closed field is called reductive if it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup; unipotent means that in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation its geometric points $u$ satisfy $(u-I)^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$. If $\bar k$ and $\bar L$ are any algebraic closures of $k$ and $L$, respectively, then
$$G_{\bar k}^0\text{ is reductive}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G_{\bar L}^0\text{ is reductive}.$$
The same equivalence holds with any algebraically closed extensions of $k$ and $L$ in place of their algebraic closures. Thus, for a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation $H\to S$ over a scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the subset $U(H/S)$ of points whose geometric fibre has reductive identity component satisfies $U(H\times_ST/T)=g^{-1}(U(H/S))$ for every morphism $g:T\to S$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Exercise 3.4.1(i)-(iii), printed p.104 (ascent of reductivity under extensions of algebraically closed fields), and the pullback assertion in the proof of Corollary 3.1.11, printed p.89; Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), Proposition 1.34, printed pp.16-17 (identity components commute with field extension). Conrad PDF WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf. No Stacks tag states the reductivity assertion.

proof.text: First let $F\subseteq E$ be algebraically closed fields and $J/F$ smooth connected affine of finite type. If $J$ is not reductive, choose a nontrivial smooth connected closed normal unipotent subgroup $N\subseteq J$. Its scalar extension $N_E$ is smooth by lem-pc-proper-base-change(2), and closed in $J_E$ by lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change. It is connected by lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component: since $N=N^0$, its scalar extension is the identity component of $N_E$. Normality is the original normality assertion tested on $E$-algebras, which are also $F$-algebras. Base change of a faithful matrix embedding remains closed and its geometric matrices remain unipotent, since every algebraically closed extension of $E$ is one of $F$. Finally $N_E\ne1$: the nonzero augmentation ideal of $F[N]$ stays nonzero under tensoring with $E$, because a basis of an $F$-vector space stays linearly independent after extension of scalars. Thus $J_E$ is not reductive.

source.place: Proposition 19.13, easy direction; Proposition 1.34 for connectedness; geometric matrix definition of unipotence

proof.text: Conversely suppose $J_E$ is not reductive, and choose a nontrivial smooth connected closed normal unipotent subgroup $N\subseteq J_E$. Apply lem-sfb-normal-unipotent-subgroup-spreading to $F\subseteq E$, $J$ and this specified $N$. It supplies a finitely generated $F$-subalgebra $A\subseteq E$ and a closed normal model $\mathcal N\subseteq J_A$ whose every geometric fibre is nontrivial smooth connected unipotent. The ring $A$ is nonzero because it is a subring of a field. Choose a maximal ideal of $A$. By lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing(1), its residue field is $F$, so there is an $F$-algebra homomorphism $a:A\to F$. The fibre $\mathcal N_a\subseteq J$ furnished by the spreading statement is a nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Therefore $J$ is not reductive. Together with step 1 this proves $J$ reductive if and only if $J_E$ is reductive.

source.place: Exercise 3.4.1(i)-(iii), printed p.104; specialization at a rational closed point

proof.text: Now let $k$ be arbitrary and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$. For any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, extend $k\to\Omega$ to $\bar k\to\Omega$ using lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed. By lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component, $C=G_{\bar k}^0$ is an open and closed finite-type subgroup and $C_\Omega=(G_\Omega)^0$. It is connected by its definition; it is affine as a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $G_{\bar k}$. It is smooth as an open subscheme of the smooth scheme $G_{\bar k}$: a smooth local chart for the latter restricts to a smooth chart for the open. Smoothness of $G_{\bar k}$ follows from lem-pc-proper-base-change(2). Apply steps 1 and 2 to $C/\bar k$ and $\Omega/\bar k$. This proves that $G_\Omega^0$ is reductive precisely when $G_{\bar k}^0$ is reductive, independently of the chosen embedding of $\bar k$.

source.place: Propositions 1.34 and 19.13; algebraic-closure embedding: Stacks fields.tex Tag 09GU, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure

proof.text: An algebraically closed extension of $L$ is also an algebraically closed extension of $k$ through $k\to L$. Apply step 3 to each of the two algebraically closed fields being compared. Both reductivity assertions are equivalent to reductivity of $G_{\bar k}^0$. Taking the second field to be $\bar L$ gives the first displayed equivalence; allowing arbitrary algebraically closed extensions gives the second. This uses no connectedness assumption on $G$.

source.place: Proposition 19.13 applied after Proposition 1.34; logical assembly

proof.text: Finally let $t\in T$, $s=g(t)$. The local homomorphism on stalks induces a field embedding $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$. The fibre of $H_T$ at $t$ is canonically $H_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$: both sides represent pairs of points of $H$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ with equal images in $S$. Smoothness of $H_s$ follows from lem-pc-proper-base-change(2). Affineness is preserved on affine charts by the tensor-product description of fibre products, and finite presentation is preserved by tensoring its finite lists of generators and relations. Thus $H_s$ is a smooth affine finite-type group over the field $\kappa(s)$. Step 4 says that its geometric identity component is reductive exactly when the geometric identity component of its scalar extension to $\kappa(t)$ is. Hence $t\in U(H_T/T)$ if and only if $s\in U(H/S)$. Equality of these memberships for every $t$ is the required pullback equality.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, pullback identity in its proof, printed p.89; pointwise fibre-product argument
